snapback4.verdict: The authorized local replica collapsed live, offline, and multi-device into schema, then billed that gift back as an examined-row ceiling on expiring unique indexes.
snapback4.would_use_again_for: A WhatsApp-shaped multi-device client where devices hold the chat; not a 10k-message group that also needs server expire-at on the same table.

overall.note: M1–M6 and M8 web-green on reactive queries, file storage, and crons; password auth, offline outbox, and wall-clock queries were hand-rolled; scale verification stayed PENDING after a 32k read limit.

setup_and_docs.note: CONVEX_AGENT_MODE=anonymous plus hidden --local-cloud-port flags bound 55501/55502 without an account; second-instance BadAdminKey was not on the README happy path.

data_modeling.note: TypeScript defineSchema plus indexes in convex/schema.ts expressed Clique without SQL; receipts, unread, and word-prefix search were extra tables and aggregations, not primitives.

authorization.note: No first-class session in the query layer: every follow/send/like threads a token through requireSession; membership and edit windows are per-mutation ifs, not a policy language.

queries_and_live.note: useQuery made M1 profile edits, M2 likes, M3 DMs, and M8 device-2 live without channels; queries do not re-run when Date.now() crosses typing/expiry, so client timers hid them.

writes_and_transactions.note: Mutations plus clientIds gave idempotent set-state; optional validators reject null so M3 send with mediaStorageId:null never ran (convex-defect knowledge-gap); no bulk insert for the action log.

offline_sync.note: Essay: Convex is online-first; src/offline.ts is a localStorage queue and search corpus; M6 web flush passed after a navigator.onLine poll, not a platform outbox.

media_assets.note: generateUploadUrl → POST → storage.getUrl covered avatars, chat media, and backgrounds with no bucket policy; view-once/tombstone denial is mediaMeta plus HTTP /api/file refusal.

background_work.note: M8 digest is crons.interval plus isReplayMode; pushLogs is an ordinary table; no-connected-client and disappearing expiry are presence rows and read-time filters, not a clocked query.

client_integration.note: useQuery is the Expo subscription; custom-client is ConvexHttpClient; hooks take tokens rather than a session; Metro stale bundles required expo start --clear (environment).

diagnostics_dev_loop.note: Null-versus-undefined validators failed closed with an idle UI; runtime.counts collect() threw Many documents read at 32k (convex-defect); function reload was fast, the web bundle was not.

scale_and_limits.note: run-log convex-defect: collect() hits the 32k-document read limit at scale checkpoints; final-report scale end/verification PENDING; write path is a 167k HTTP mutation firehose with no COPY.

operations.note: A second anonymous instance was a new directory and sqlite file on 55503/55504; copying config.json’s admin key 401’d; dashboard URL printed null; seed is mutation replay.

convex.verdict: Reactive queries and crons made the two-client messenger cheap, while auth, offline, and wall-clock expiry stayed application code and scale hit a 32k read ceiling.
convex.would_use_again_for: A live two-client Clique where subscriptions matter more than built-in auth, a durable outbox, or restoring 100k messages from backup.

overall.note: Auth and SQL invariants carried M1–M2; the rest was a 1643-line BFF with polls and a localStorage queue; M3 choreography aborted on Expo plumbing, with Realtime unused.

setup_and_docs.note: Hosted Auth docs paid M1 rent; no CLI/local stack, so DDL and Realtime publication went through the pooled URL; createUser wrapped duplicate handle as Database error creating new user.

data_modeling.note: UNIQUE handle, dm_pair, membership-at-send, and digest (user_id, period_start) are SQL; the server program is server/store.mjs (~1643 lines) because RLS/RPC felt like more ceremony.

authorization.note: Password JWTs and logout revocation are the provider path; membership, edit windows, and media denial ran in authorizeMedia/store with the service role, not RLS policies.

queries_and_live.note: Feeds paginated in SQL; live path was 1s/200ms/700ms HTTP polls because postgres_changes/broadcast were not trusted from docs; M3 typing missed the 2s window.

writes_and_transactions.note: SQL UNIQUE mutation_id and now() windows; register was Auth createUser then a profile row, not one mutation; store functions are explicit and idempotent via seenMutation.

offline_sync.note: supabase-js 2.112.4 has no mutation outbox matching the brief; src/lib/offline.ts is localStorage; M6 web queue choreography never greened (blocked-by-M3).

media_assets.note: Private bucket plus path-on-row is the happy path; revocation required streaming through authorizeMedia with the service role so signed URLs could not outlive view-once/tombstone.

background_work.note: Digest is setInterval in the API process every 5s, not pg_cron (no CLI); push_log when no fresh device; presence heartbeats are application tables.

client_integration.note: supabase-js persistSession handled M1 restart; the Expo app still called a homegrown HTTP API; Realtime client unused; load-on-mount raced session restore (401).

diagnostics_dev_loop.note: Postgres $1 type errors were immediate; Auth hid handle collisions; hosted pooler EMAXCONNSESSION hit m8-a05 while suite and choreography shared session-mode clients.

scale_and_limits.note: Replay on prefix clq916g_s_ stopped before the 10% checkpoint; hosted session pooler EMAXCONNSESSION is the experienced ceiling; SQL itself never refused the 10kth group message.

operations.note: Prefix schema plus cleanup.mjs dropped 48 objects; Auth users cannot be prefix-dropped on the shared hosted project; no CLI; a second instance is another prefix and bucket.

supabase.verdict: Postgres and Auth made invariants and signup boring; Clique’s session-shaped live/offline/jobs work became a BFF plus polls on a hosted project with no CLI.
supabase.would_use_again_for: The follow graph, unique DMs, and digest key in SQL—not typing, offline queues, or a bakeoff against runtimes that already are the client replica.

cross_backend_notes: Snapback was the only published surface that already was the brief’s replica, outbox, typed assets, and jobs; Convex and Supabase both rebuilt queues and extra tables in application code.

Outcome splits are not one kind of finding: Supabase’s M3 abort is mostly Expo/Playwright (agent-error), while Snapback’s expire-at drop and Convex’s 32k collect() are platform ceilings on a product-preserving design.
Live updates separated Snapback and Convex (default reactive queries) from Supabase, which shipped 200ms/700ms HTTP polls after Realtime was not trusted from docs at the point of need.
Auth inverted that ranking: Supabase Auth and Snapback password identity were products; Convex bcrypt plus a sessions table was brief-legal and still a gap on every subsequent verb.

Local vs hosted posture showed up in operations: Snapback and Convex spun a second directory instance; the shared Supabase project could not namespace Auth users and hit session-pooler EMAXCONNSESSION.
